source._php_version_note: public/admin/environment.xml (Moodle 5.2) and public/lib/phpminimumversionlib.php require PHP >= 8.3.0, as does composer.json. Since 2026-10-10 the image runs Ubuntu 24.04's own PHP 8.3 (it reports 8.3.6; Ubuntu backports security fixes into it) instead of the official php:8.4-apache-bookworm image, whose Debian 12 base our cerodeo-v1 scan grades F on vulnerabilities Debian does not fix. That is exactly Moodle 5.2's floor, so a Moodle release that raises it cannot run on this image. PHP 8.4 on Ubuntu 24.04 would need a third-party archive (a PPA): a supply-chain decision, not taken here; preflight check_php BLOCKs a retarget whose source needs more than the image's PHP.
source._ext_note: Moodle 5.2 extensions (public/admin/environment.xml): required iconv mbstring curl openssl ctype zip zlib gd simplexml spl pcre dom xml xmlreader intl json hash fileinfo sodium filter, optional tokenizer soap exif; plus the NATIVE mysqli driver (lib/dml/mysqli_native_moodle_database.php, NOT pdo_mysql) and opcache. source.php_extensions lists exactly these and the build asserts each is loaded in both the Apache and the CLI configuration. They come from Ubuntu's packages (runtime_packages): php8.3-gd, -intl, -zip, -soap, -mysql (which also carries pdo_mysql, unused by Moodle), -curl, -mbstring, -xml; sodium and opcache with php8.3-cli, exif/iconv/ctype/fileinfo/tokenizer with php8.3-common. Nothing is compiled.
source._app_copies_note: Copy the WHOLE Moodle tree to /var/www/html — the app spans root-level admin/ (incl admin/cli/install.php), lib/, config-dist.php AND public/ (the webroot). NO composer vendor/ dir to copy (Moodle's runtime PHP libs are already in-tree under public/lib/). NO composer_install_cmd => the renderer emits no composer step. NO frontend block => no npm/grunt (AMD assets pre-built in the tag).
